newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria president backs NATO referendum - paper.
newsitem.headline: Austria president backs NATO referendum - paper.

text.p: President Thomas Klestil said in a newspaper interview he supported holding a referendum to decide whether neutral Austria should join the NATO military alliance.
"NATO membership is such a crucial question for our country, that it is justifiable to consider asking the nation," Klestil told the daily Kurier in its advance Thursday edition.
Austria's uneasy ruling coalition of Social Democrats and conservative People's Party is at loggerheads over the issue of whether to join the 16-nation Western alliance.
The Social Democrats of Chancellor Viktor Klima want Austria to remain neutral, although Klima has said any decision on membership had to be put before the nation.

Foreign Minister Wolfgang Schuessel's conservatives insist Austria must move with the times, saying that the near-certainty Poland, the Czech Republic and Hungary will be selected as new candidates in the first wave of NATO's enlargement at a summit in Madrid in July meant Vienna had to decide as soon as possible.
But Schuessel's People's Party have opposed holding a referendum on NATO.

Neutrality was enshrined in the constitution on the insistence of the Kremlin, which refused to pull its occupying troops out of Austria in 1955 unless the country swore off any membership of military alliances.
Austria was occupied by World War Two's victors after its defeat alongside Nazi Germany in 1945.
